```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

```{r model-load}
mod <- readModelDb("vandeKreeke_2026_antibiotic_immune_bacteremia")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
```

* Citation: `r ui$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s10928-026-10063-6>
* Open-access full text: <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC13597578/>
* Supplements: Online Resource 1 (Tables S1-S3, Figs. S1-S4), Online
  Resources 2 and 3 (in vitro neutrophil and monocyte sub-fits) and Online
  Resource 4 (mouse calibration).
* Description: `r ui$description`

The model is a generic host-pathogen model. No named drug or pathogen is
modelled: the bacteria are a homogeneous population with MIC 1 mg/L, and the
antibiotic is a hypothetical agent with one-compartment PK (V 5 L, half-life
5 h). Four antibiotic types are produced by two parameters of the Regoes 2004
growth-rate function: `kgmin` (-1 1/h bacteriostatic, -3 1/h bactericidal) and
`hill` (0.5 time-dependent, 3 concentration-dependent). The packaged default is
bacteriostatic time-dependent; the other types are selected by overriding
`kgmin` and `lhill`.

Three per-subject inputs are required:

* `NEUT`: absolute neutrophil count (cells/mm^3), constant over time;
* `MONO_ABS`: absolute monocyte count (cells/mm^3), constant over time;
* `MIC`: the MIC of the antibiotic against the bacterium (mg/L).

The bacterial inoculum is given as a dose (CFU/mL) into `bact_susceptible` at
time zero, and the antibiotic dose (mg) into `central`. The output `cfu` is the
extracellular bacterial density of Eq. 1, which is the quantity the paper plots
(see "Bacterial density output" below); `cfu_total` adds the bacteria still held
inside phagocytes.

# Population

No patient data were fitted. The phagocytosis and digestion parameters were
estimated from digitised in vitro time-courses of bacteria incubated with
neutrophils or monocytes (Online Resource 1, Table S2), and a single scaling
factor on both maximum phagocytosis rates (0.227, RSE 2.77%) was estimated from
24-h blood CFU counts in four immune-competent mice inoculated intravenously
with *E. coli* (Table S3, Online Resource 4). The calibrated model was then used
to simulate adults with bacteremia in seven immune states (Methods, Evaluation
of immune status on PKPD targets):

```{r immune-states}
immune_states <- tibble::tribble(
  ~state,                                 ~NEUT, ~MONO_ABS,
  "Immune competent",                      5000,       600,
  "Monocytopenia",                         5000,       200,
  "Mild neutropenia",                      1250,       600,
  "Moderate neutropenia",                   750,       600,
  "Severe neutropenia",                     500,       600,
  "Severe neutropenia & monocytopenia",     500,       200,
  "Fully immune compromised",                 0,         0
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(state = factor(state, levels = state))

antibiotic_types <- tibble::tribble(
  ~type,                                      ~kgmin, ~hill,
  "Bacteriostatic\ntime dependent",              -1,   0.5,
  "Bactericidal\ntime dependent",                -3,   0.5,
  "Bacteriostatic\nconcentration dependent",     -1,   3,
  "Bactericidal\nconcentration dependent",       -3,   3
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(type = factor(type, levels = type))

immune_states |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    "Neutrophils (cells/mL)" = NEUT * 1000,
    "Monocytes (cells/mL)" = MONO_ABS * 1000
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Immune state" = state,
    "NEUT (cells/mm^3)" = NEUT,
    "MONO_ABS (cells/mm^3)" = MONO_ABS
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Immune states simulated in the paper (Methods).")
```

# Simulation helpers

Every simulation below is deterministic: the model has no between-subject
variability and no residual error. Each row of a scenario grid becomes one
subject; the scenario's covariates and antibiotic-type parameters are carried
as data columns, which `rxSolve()` uses in place of the `ini()` values.

```{r helpers}
# One subject per scenario row. `dose` is the total daily antibiotic dose (mg),
# split into `n_doses` equal boluses over 24 h; `b0` is the inoculum (CFU/mL).
build_events <- function(scen, obs_times) {
  scen$id <- seq_len(nrow(scen))
  inoc <- data.frame(id = scen$id, time = 0, amt = scen$b0, cmt = "bact_susceptible", evid = 1L)
  obs <- expand.grid(id = scen$id, time = obs_times)
  obs <- data.frame(id = obs$id, time = obs$time, amt = 0, cmt = "bact_susceptible", evid = 0L)
  ev <- rbind(inoc, obs)
  abx <- scen[scen$dose > 0, c("id", "dose", "n_doses")]
  if (nrow(abx) > 0) {
    abx <- abx[rep(seq_len(nrow(abx)), abx$n_doses), ]
    dose_index <- stats::ave(abx$id, abx$id, FUN = seq_along) - 1
    ev <- rbind(ev, data.frame(
      id = abx$id, time = dose_index * 24 / abx$n_doses,
      amt = abx$dose / abx$n_doses, cmt = "central", evid = 1L
    ))
  }
  covs <- scen[, c("id", "NEUT", "MONO_ABS", "MIC", "kgmin", "lhill", "lkgrowth")]
  ev <- merge(ev, covs, by = "id")
  ev <- ev[order(ev$id, ev$time, -ev$evid), ]
  list(events = ev, scen = scen)
}

simulate_grid <- function(scen, obs_times) {
  b <- build_events(scen, obs_times)
  sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, b$events, returnType = "data.frame", atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10)
  # rxSolve() omits the id column when there is only one subject.
  if (!"id" %in% names(sim)) sim$id <- 1L
  sim <- sim[, c("id", "time", "Cc", "cfu", "cfu_total")]
  dplyr::left_join(sim, b$scen, by = "id")
}

# The paper's plots stop at about 10^-3.7 CFU/mL; values below are shown at
# that floor.
plot_floor <- 10^-3.7
default_type <- data.frame(kgmin = -1, lhill = log(0.5))
```

# Antibiotic PK check

The PK component is a one-compartment bolus model, so a single 100 mg dose has
the closed form `C(t) = 20 * exp(-ln(2) t / 5)` mg/L.

```{r pk-check}
pk_scen <- data.frame(
  NEUT = 0, MONO_ABS = 0, MIC = 1, dose = 100, n_doses = 1, b0 = 0,
  lkgrowth = log(0.9), default_type, treatment = "100 mg IV bolus"
)
pk_sim <- simulate_grid(pk_scen, obs_times = seq(0, 48, by = 0.5))
closed_form <- 100 / 5 * exp(-log(2) / 5 * pk_sim$time)
stopifnot(max(abs(pk_sim$Cc - closed_form) / closed_form) < 1e-6)

conc <- pk_sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_df <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = 100, treatment = "100 mg IV bolus")
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id, route = "intravascular")
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

simulated_nca <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)

# Methods: V = 5 L and half-life 5 h, so Cmax = 100 / 5 mg/L and
# AUCinf = dose / CL = 100 / (5 * ln(2) / 5) mg*h/L.
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,        ~PPTESTCD,    ~PPORRES,
  "100 mg IV bolus", "cmax",       100 / 5,
  "100 mg IV bolus", "aucinf.obs", 100 / log(2),
  "100 mg IV bolus", "half.life",  5
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = simulated_nca,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", aucinf.obs = "mg*h/L", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "PKNCA on the simulated antibiotic profile against the PK stated in the Methods (V 5 L, half-life 5 h).")
```

# Bacterial dynamics without antibiotic (Online Resource 1, Fig. S1)

Fig. S1 simulates each immune state with inocula of 10^5 to 10^9 CFU/mL and no
antibiotic, for four growth rates. The two rows reproduced here are
`kgrw = 0.9` 1/h (the value carried forward to the dose-fractionation
simulations) and `kgrw = 0.5885` 1/h (the in vivo value used in the
calibration).

```{r fig-s1, fig.height = 5.5}
s1_scen <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  immune_states,
  b0 = 10^(5:9),
  kgrw = c(0.5885, 0.9)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(MIC = 1, dose = 0, n_doses = 1, lkgrowth = log(kgrw), kgmin = -1, lhill = log(0.5)) |>
  as.data.frame()
s1_sim <- simulate_grid(s1_scen, obs_times = seq(0, 24, by = 0.25))

ggplot(s1_sim, aes(time, pmax(cfu, plot_floor), colour = factor(b0), group = id)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_grid(paste("kgrw", kgrw) ~ state, labeller = label_wrap_gen(14)) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = 10^seq(-3, 9, by = 2)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Bacterial density (CFU/mL)", colour = "Inoculum (CFU/mL)",
    caption = "Replicates Online Resource 1, Fig. S1 (rows kgrw = 0.5885 and 0.9) of van de Kreeke 2026."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text = element_text(size = 7))
```

The table compares the log10 density at 24 h for `kgrw = 0.9` 1/h with values
read by the maintainers off Fig. S1 (bottom row). "cleared" means the curve
reached the plot floor (about 10^-3.7 CFU/mL) before 24 h.

```{r fig-s1-table}
s1_paper <- tibble::tribble(
  ~state,                                ~b0,  ~paper,
  "Immune competent",                     1e5, "cleared (about 9.5 h)",
  "Immune competent",                     1e6, "cleared (about 11 h)",
  "Immune competent",                     1e7, "cleared (about 14 h)",
  "Immune competent",                     1e8, "about -0.6",
  "Immune competent",                     1e9, "about 9.2",
  "Monocytopenia",                        1e6, "cleared (about 16 h)",
  "Monocytopenia",                        1e7, "cleared (about 21 h)",
  "Monocytopenia",                        1e8, "about 9.2",
  "Mild neutropenia",                     1e6, "cleared (about 14 h)",
  "Mild neutropenia",                     1e7, "cleared (about 23 h)",
  "Moderate neutropenia",                 1e6, "cleared (about 18 h)",
  "Moderate neutropenia",                 1e7, "about 4",
  "Severe neutropenia",                   1e5, "cleared (about 19 h)",
  "Severe neutropenia",                   1e6, "cleared (about 23 h)",
  "Severe neutropenia & monocytopenia",   1e5, "about -1.2",
  "Severe neutropenia & monocytopenia",   1e6, "about 3.5",
  "Fully immune compromised",             1e5, "about 9.2"
)

# Time at which the density first falls to the plot floor.
time_cleared <- s1_sim |>
  dplyr::filter(kgrw == 0.9) |>
  dplyr::group_by(state, b0) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    t_floor = if (any(cfu <= plot_floor)) min(time[cfu <= plot_floor]) else NA_real_,
    log10_24 = log10(max(cfu[time == 24], plot_floor)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

s1_cmp <- s1_paper |>
  dplyr::mutate(state = factor(state, levels = levels(immune_states$state))) |>
  dplyr::left_join(time_cleared, by = c("state", "b0")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    packaged = ifelse(
      is.na(t_floor),
      sprintf("%.1f", log10_24),
      sprintf("cleared (%.1f h)", t_floor)
    )
  )
s1_cmp |>
  dplyr::select(state, b0, paper, packaged) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Immune state" = state,
    "Inoculum (CFU/mL)" = b0,
    "Paper Fig. S1: log10 CFU/mL at 24 h" = paper,
    "Packaged model: log10 CFU/mL at 24 h" = packaged
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Fig. S1, kgrw = 0.9 1/h: paper (read off the figure) against the packaged model.")

# Low-inoculum immune clearance agrees: immune-competent 10^5 and 10^6 CFU/mL
# reach the floor within about 1.5 h of the paper's curves.
comp_low <- time_cleared |>
  dplyr::filter(state == "Immune competent", b0 %in% c(1e5, 1e6))
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(comp_low$t_floor),
  all(abs(comp_low$t_floor - c(9.5, 11)) < 1.5)
)
```

At low inocula the packaged model clears bacteria on the paper's timescale. At
high inocula it clears too little: for example, immune-competent 10^8 CFU/mL
and mild neutropenia at 10^7 CFU/mL grow towards `Bmax` here but are cleared in
Fig. S1. The mismatch is discussed under "Assumptions and deviations".

# Dose fractionation (Fig. 3 and Online Resource 1, Fig. S2)

Each immune state and antibiotic type is simulated with a 10^9 CFU/mL
inoculum, `kgrw = 0.9` 1/h, and total daily doses of 0-100 mg given as 1, 2, 3
or 6 boluses. The output is the bacterial density at 24 h.

```{r fig-3, fig.height = 9}
f3_scen <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  immune_states,
  antibiotic_types,
  n_doses = c(1, 2, 3, 6),
  dose = seq(0, 100, by = 5)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    MIC = 1, b0 = 1e9, lkgrowth = log(0.9), lhill = log(hill),
    interval = factor(24 / n_doses, levels = c(4, 8, 12, 24))
  ) |>
  as.data.frame()
f3_sim <- simulate_grid(f3_scen, obs_times = 24)

ggplot(f3_sim, aes(dose, pmax(cfu, plot_floor), colour = interval)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1e7, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_grid(state ~ type, labeller = label_wrap_gen(16)) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = 10^seq(-3, 9, by = 2)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("4" = "red", "8" = "blue", "12" = "orange", "24" = "darkgreen")) +
  labs(
    x = "Total dose (mg)", y = "Bacterial density at 24 h (CFU/mL)", colour = "Interval (h)",
    caption = "Replicates Fig. 3 of van de Kreeke 2026 (all seven immune states, as in Online Resource 1, Fig. S2)."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text = element_text(size = 7))
```

# Dose for a 2-log10 drop (Fig. 4a)

The dose giving a 2-log10 reduction (10^9 to 10^7 CFU/mL at 24 h) is found here
for a single dose (24-h interval) by interpolating log10 density over a 1-mg
dose grid, as Fig. 4a does for doses given once.

```{r fig-4a}
f4_scen <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  immune_states,
  antibiotic_types,
  dose = seq(0, 200, by = 1)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(MIC = 1, b0 = 1e9, n_doses = 1, lkgrowth = log(0.9), lhill = log(hill)) |>
  as.data.frame()
f4_sim <- simulate_grid(f4_scen, obs_times = 24)

dose_2log <- f4_sim |>
  dplyr::mutate(l10 = log10(pmax(cfu, 1e-12))) |>
  dplyr::group_by(state, type) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    dose_2log = {
      i <- which(l10 <= 7)[1]
      if (is.na(i) || i == 1) NA_real_ else dose[i - 1] + (7 - l10[i - 1]) / (l10[i] - l10[i - 1]) * (dose[i] - dose[i - 1])
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(type) |>
  dplyr::mutate(fc = dose_2log / dose_2log[state == "Immune competent"]) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
stopifnot(!anyNA(dose_2log$dose_2log))
```

The fully immune-compromised state has no immune clearance, so it isolates
the antibiotic PK/PD half of the model. Its single-dose 2-log10 doses agree
with those read off the bottom row of Fig. 3 (24-h curve crossing 10^7 CFU/mL):

```{r fig-4a-pkpd}
fig3_none <- tibble::tribble(
  ~type,                                      ~paper_dose,
  "Bacteriostatic\ntime dependent",            66,
  "Bactericidal\ntime dependent",              42,
  "Bacteriostatic\nconcentration dependent",   37,
  "Bactericidal\nconcentration dependent",     19
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(type = factor(type, levels = levels(antibiotic_types$type)))

none_cmp <- dose_2log |>
  dplyr::filter(state == "Fully immune compromised") |>
  dplyr::left_join(fig3_none, by = "type") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (dose_2log - paper_dose) / paper_dose)

none_cmp |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    type = gsub("\n", " ", type),
    paper_dose, dose_2log = round(dose_2log, 1), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Antibiotic type" = type,
    "Paper Fig. 3 (mg, read off the figure)" = paper_dose,
    "Packaged model (mg)" = dose_2log,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Fully immune compromised, single dose: dose giving a 2-log10 drop at 24 h.")

# Figure reading is good to a few mg on a 0-100 mg axis.
stopifnot(all(abs(none_cmp$pct_diff) < 20))
```

With immune cells present the fold-changes against the immune-competent state
differ from Fig. 4a. The packaged model needs a larger immune-competent dose
than the paper (for example about 13 mg rather than about 5 mg for the
bacteriostatic time-dependent type, Fig. 3 top row), because its immune
clearance at a 10^9 CFU/mL load is weaker. As a result the fully
immune-compromised and the severe neutropenia with monocytopenia fold-changes
are smaller than published, monocytopenia has no effect at all (fold change 1),
and adding monocytopenia to severe neutropenia changes nothing. For the
concentration-dependent types the mild to severe neutropenia fold-changes come
out somewhat larger than published. The published fold-changes below were read
off Fig. 4a by the maintainers, except the two fully-immune-compromised values
that the Results text states (25.5 and 5.7).

```{r fig-4a-table}
  dplyr::transmute(
    type = gsub("\n", " ", type), state, paper_fc,
    fc = round(fc, 2), dose_2log = round(dose_2log, 1)
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Antibiotic type" = type,
    "Immune state" = state,
    "Paper fold change (Fig. 4a)" = paper_fc,
    "Packaged fold change" = fc,
    "Packaged single dose for 2-log10 drop (mg)" = dose_2log
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Fold change in the single dose needed for a 2-log10 drop, against the immune-competent state.")

fc_long <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::transmute(fc_cmp, state, type, fc = paper_fc, source = "Paper (Fig. 4a)"),
  dplyr::transmute(fc_cmp, state, type, fc, source = "Packaged model")
)
ggplot(fc_long, aes(state, fc, fill = source)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  facet_wrap(~type, nrow = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(trans = "log2") +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Fold change in dose", fill = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Fig. 4a of van de Kreeke 2026."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 7), legend.position = "bottom")
```

Fig. 4b (the change in %T>MIC or AUC/MIC targets) is not reproduced: those
targets come from curves the authors fitted to bacterial density against the
PK/PD index across all four dosing intervals (Online Resource 1, Fig. S3), and
the functional form of those fits is not reported.

# Mouse calibration (Online Resource 4)

The calibration simulates immune-competent mice (neutrophils 1.7 x 10^5 and
monocytes 1.4 x 10^6 cells/mL, Table S3), an inoculum of 1.6 x 10^7 CFU/mL and
`kgrw = 0.5885` 1/h (Results, Calibration). In Online Resource 4, Figure 2 the
calibrated model stays near 10^7 CFU/mL over 24 h (observed 24-h values
about 2 x 10^6 to 2 x 10^7 CFU/mL).

```{r mouse}
mouse_scen <- data.frame(
  NEUT = 170, MONO_ABS = 1400, MIC = 1, dose = 0, n_doses = 1, b0 = 1.6e7,
  lkgrowth = log(0.5885), default_type
)
mouse_sim <- simulate_grid(mouse_scen, obs_times = seq(0, 24, by = 0.5))
ggplot(mouse_sim, aes(time, cfu)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 23.5, xmax = 24.5, ymin = 2e6, ymax = 2.2e7, alpha = 0.3, fill = "red") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Bacteria (CFU/mL)",
    caption = paste(
      "Packaged model for the calibration scenario; shaded: range of the four",
      "observed 24-h values in Online Resource 4, Figure 1."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The packaged model grows towards `Bmax` in this scenario (24-h density
`r format(signif(mouse_sim$cfu[mouse_sim$time == 24], 2), scientific = TRUE)` CFU/mL) instead of staying
near the observed values: it is the same high-load under-prediction of immune
clearance seen in Fig. S1.

# Bacterial density output

```{r output-check}
comp_tot <- f3_sim |>
  dplyr::filter(state == "Immune competent", dose == 100, n_doses == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(type, cfu, cfu_total)
knitr::kable(comp_tot, caption = "Immune competent, 100 mg once: extracellular and total bacteria at 24 h (CFU/mL).")
```

The paper's Figs. 3 and S1 curves reach the plot floor in the immune-competent
state. Only the extracellular bacteria do that here; the total including
intracellular bacteria stays at a few times 10^6 CFU/mL because the monocyte pool
saturates (B_M/M well above `B_M/Md50` with the steep `gamma_d = 14` digestion
term), so the figures plot the extracellular `cfu`.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Typographical errors corrected.** Eq. 9 prints `B/N` (extracellular
  bacteria per neutrophil) in the last term of the capacity denominator, and
  Eqs. 11 and 12 print `B/M`; the numerators and the half-maximum parameters
  are intracellular ratios (B_N/N, B_M/M; Table 1 units CFU/cell). The packaged
  model uses the intracellular ratio throughout, as in Eq. 8, the general form
  Eq. 4 and the Thorsted 2023 neutrophil model the structure comes from. Taken
  literally, the printed form lets intracellular bacteria accumulate above
  `Bmax` and the solve fails.
* **Intracellular-pool equations written from Fig. 1.** The paper prints no
  equation for the intracellular bacteria. Each pool gains bacteria by
  phagocytosis (`knp * B`, `kmp * B`) and loses them by digestion
  (`knd * B_N`, `kmd * B_M`), as drawn in Fig. 1.
* **Calibrated structure.** Neutrophil apoptosis, phagocytosis-induced death
  and the monocyte time-driven decay (Eqs. 5, 6, 10 and the exponential factors
  of Eqs. 11-12) were removed for the in vivo model (Methods, Calibration), so
  the immune-cell counts are constant covariates.
* **High-load immune clearance is under-predicted.** The antibiotic PK/PD half
  of the model reproduces the paper (fully immune-compromised doses for a
  2-log10 drop within 20% of Fig. 3), and so does immune clearance at low
  inocula (Fig. S1, 10^5-10^6 CFU/mL). At high bacterial loads, where the
  intracellular capacity terms saturate, the packaged model clears several-fold
  fewer bacteria than the paper's own simulations: Fig. S1 (immune-competent
  10^8, mild neutropenia 10^7, severe neutropenia with monocytopenia 10^6
  CFU/mL), the mouse calibration (Online Resource 4) and the immune-competent
  doses of Fig. 3. Consequently the Fig. 4a fold-changes are not reproduced
  (most are smaller than published), and monocytopenia has no effect at a
  10^9 CFU/mL load here whereas Fig. 4a shows a 1.1- to 2.3-fold dose
  increase. No uniform change to
  the printed capacity terms reproduces every panel, so the difference
  presumably lies in the authors' code, which the paper states is available on
  request. The model is shipped as printed (with the corrections above) and no
  parameter has been tuned to the figures.
* **Bacterial density output.** `cfu` is the extracellular density of Eq. 1;
  see the previous section.
* **Default antibiotic type.** The paper has no default; the packaged values
  `kgmin = -1` and `hill = 0.5` (bacteriostatic, time dependent) are one of its
  four types.
* **knp,max and kmp,max.** Table 1 (1.90 and 1.77 1/h) is used; Online
  Resource 4 gives 1.895 and 1.766 1/h from the in vitro values times the
  scaling factor 0.227. Online Resource 4 prints the unit as CFU/mL/h; Table 1
  gives 1/h, which is what first-order Eq. 1 requires.
* **Published comparison values** for Figs. 3, 4a and S1 were read off the
  figures by the maintainers and are approximate.
